header.running_head: Things that Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) Disliked Happening in the Masjid

blocks.text: Masjid when someone threw a pebble at him. When he looked up, he saw that it was Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to him, "Go and bring those two men to me." When Hadhrat Saa'ib (RA) brought them, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked them who they were. "We are from Taa'if," they replied. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "Had you been from this town (Madinah), I would have certainly punished you. How can you raise your voices in the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ?" [^1]

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Ibraheem reports from his father that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) heard someone speaking in the Masjid, he asked, "Do you know where you are? Do you know where you are?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) dislikes hearing people speak (loudly) in the Masjid. [^2]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that whenever Hadhrat Umar (RA) went to the Masjid, he announced in the Masjid, "Do refrain from making a noise." Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) would announce at the top of his voice, "Refrain from futilities in the Masjid!" [^3]
It is reported that Hadhrat Umar (RA) forbade noise in the Masjid saying, "Voices should never be raised in our Masaajid." [^4]

Hadhrat Saalim narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) had a platform built next to the Masjid, which he called Butayhaa. He would then say, "Whoever wishes to make a noise, to recite a poem or to raise his voice should go to the platform." [^5]

Hadhrat Taariq bin Shihaab narrates that it was in the Masjid that a person was brought before Hadhrat Umar (RA) for some crime. Hadhrat Umar (RA) gave instructions that the man be taken out of the Masjid before being given a beating. [^6]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Disapproves of Reclining Against the Wall of the Masjid in the Direction of the Qibla

It was between the Adhaan and Iqaamah of Fajr that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once saw some people reclining against the wall of the Masjid in the direction of the Qibla. He said to them, "Do not be an obstacle between the angels and their salaah." [^7]
